headline: House Prosecutors Eye Michael Poa as Hostile Witness in Duterte Impeachment Trial
seoTitle: Prosecutors Eye Michael Poa as Hostile Witness | FMB News
seoDescription: House prosecutors are considering asking the Senate Impeachment Court to treat defense lawyer and former DepEd undersecretary Michael Poa as a hostile witness.
deck: The prosecution is considering a hostile-witness request because of Poa's current defense role and his earlier work responding to audit memoranda on DepEd confidential funds.
author: FMB News Desk

sections.heading: What happened
paragraphs: The House prosecution panel is considering asking the Senate Impeachment Court to treat Michael Poa, a member of Vice President Sara Duterte's defense team and a former Department of Education undersecretary, as a hostile witness.

The Manila Times reported that prosecutors are eyeing Poa because he responded to Commission on Audit memoranda concerning DepEd confidential funds. The court, not the prosecution, would make the final determination on his witness status.

sections.heading: What the request would mean
paragraphs: A hostile-witness request is a procedural application, not a finding that Poa or the Vice President committed wrongdoing. If prosecutors formally make the request, the Senate Impeachment Court would decide whether the circumstances justify different questioning rules.

The prosecution's stated interest concerns Poa's former role at DepEd and his current position in the defense team. The evidence and any testimony remain subject to examination and challenge during the trial.

sections.heading: Context
paragraphs: The impeachment trial is examining House allegations concerning confidential funds used by the Office of the Vice President and DepEd. Duterte and her defense team have contested allegations of misuse.

Separately, financial institutions were previously given until September 2 to submit remaining records covered by Senate Impeachment Court subpoenas. Those submissions and the subpoenas themselves do not establish liability.

sections.heading: Why this matters
paragraphs: Poa's prior government role and current defense position could make his testimony important to the prosecution's effort to examine DepEd audit responses. The court's ruling would define how that examination proceeds without deciding the merits of the underlying allegations.

sections.heading: What to watch next
paragraphs: The next question is whether prosecutors formally file the request and how the defense and the Senate Impeachment Court respond. Until the court rules, Poa has not been declared a hostile witness.
